discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological insulator, the quantum spin Hall state. They introduced the Z2 invariant, which distinguishes it from ordinary insulators and guarantees protected helical edge states. Molenkamp's group confirmed the prediction in 2007 in HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, measuring quantized edge conductance that depended on well thickness as expected. This theory-experiment partnership turned Berry-curvature topology from a mathematical curiosity into a measurable, materials-based physics. It led to three-dimensional topological insulators and the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and to the search for Majorana modes. It also organized much of the band-theory classification of materials. Few ideas in the past two decades have so thoroughly changed how condensed-matter physicists think about electronic states in solids, and how many laboratories now investigate them.
